messages:
alex: Heads-up — gpu-nodegroup terraform apply finished but new GPU nodes are not joining properly. autoscaler spun them up, but kube-system CNI pods never become Ready. seeing CrashLoopBackOff and network not ready on pods scheduled to those nodes.

deploy-bot: helm upgrade failed for release=calico, namespace=kube-system: timed out waiting for the condition

mia: What AMI/akka are we using for that nodegroup? Did the CNI image get bumped in the last chart PR? :eyes:

alex: New nodegroup uses ami-2026gpu-v2 (rolled yesterday). Chart PR #342 bumped calico to v3.25.0. logs: ```
calico-node: ERROR: failed to create host endpoints: failed to set up iptables: nftables backend unsupported by kernel
Error: Failed to prepare pod network
```

sam: nft vs legacy iptables mismatch again. New AMI probably has nft default. We had this with baseline images before. Quick check: `uname -a` and `iptables --version` on the new node.

jordan: Can we cordon the new nodes and force the helm rollback to previous calico tag while we investigate? Otherwise pods keep failing and user workloads might get scheduled incorrectly.

alex: cordoned. commands run: ```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-az1-02
kubectl drain gpu-node-az1-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data -l role=worker
```

mia: I'll try a rollback to calico v3.24.1 via flux/helm. If the helm release is stuck, we may need `helm upgrade --force`.

deploy-bot: Release history: calico 1 -> upgrade -> failed -> pending rollback. kube-system events show ImagePullBackOff for calico v3.25.0-amd64.

sam: Another possibility: chart values changed `hostPorts.enabled=true` and GPU drivers require privileged hostNetwork config — check DaemonSet tolerations/privileged bits. But the nft error seems more likely.

mia: Did helm/flux try to apply CRDs during the upgrade? That can block and leave the release in a bad state. Logs show the pre-upgrade job timed out.

alex: Also noticed terraform drift: launch_template.user_data differs from what flux expects (we inject kernel boot args to prefer legacy iptables). TF applied new AMI without adding the ip_tables flag. That explains the kernel mismatch.

jordan: Short-term playbook: 1) rollback calico chart 2) mark AMI as unstable in infra registry 3) add lifecycle ignore for launch_template.user_data or patch to inject iptables-legacy boot flag 4) revert nodegroup min size to avoid idle GPUs

ops-bot: billing-alert: GPU nodes in cluster-redwood-west idle for 5.6h, estimated cost $1840 today :warning:

alex: We reduced nodegroup desired to match actual pod requests to avoid more idle nodes. Also added a temporary scaling policy to scale down quickly if CPU/GPU utilization low.

mia: Rolled calico back to v3.24.1 with `helm upgrade --install calico . --version 3.24.1 --force` and restarted DaemonSets. kube-system pods are transitioning to Running. :thumbsup:

sam: Nice. For a medium-term fix we should: - bake AMI with iptables-legacy symlink - add a preflight hook in our GitOps pipeline that checks node kernel/nettools compatibility for CNI bumps - ensure cluster-autoscaler respects gpu taints so it doesn't create lots of idle GPUs during spike tests.

jordan: Agreed. Also adding a Terraform plan check to detect launch_template.user_data drift and fail PRs that change AMI without a validated canary run. We had a similar incident last quarter.

alex: Created an incident ticket and assigned follow-ups: INFRA-487 (AMI bake + iptables fix), INFRA-488 (GitOps preflight for CNI upgrades), INFRA-489 (autoscaler gpu taint config).

mia: One extra note — Helm chart should include `podAntiAffinity` for calico-node to avoid scheduling all DaemonSet pods on new AZ at once during rollout. Will send PR for that.

sam: Also: consider adding a small canary cluster (single AZ, cheaper GPU type) to validate node AMIs and CNI upgrades before flipping prod charts.

alex: For now, everything stabilised after rollback and node drains. Lights on, but leaving cordons for 30m to ensure no stragglers. Thanks folks. :sparkles:

deploy-bot: incident INFRA-2026-03-10 created, severity=P2, start_ts=1768004321, assigned=alex,mia

jordan: Posting retrospective notes in #postmortems after incident wrap. Will include timeline and cost impact.

ops-bot: cost-summary: estimated extra spend from idle GPUs during incident: $1,920 (6.1h aggregated).

alex: Closing thread here — will follow up with PRs and the canary plan. If anyone finds stray GPU nodes, ping me. :v:
